# Pesher Psalms Column 4 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** 4QpPs (4Q171), Col. 4 | **Condition:** moderate to heavy damage

---

**4:1** "For the LORD loves justice and will not forsake His saints; they are preserved

**4:2** forever; but the seed of the wicked-ones shall be cut off" (Psalm 37:28).

**4:3** Its pesher concerns [...] the Teacher of Righteousness and those who [...] His will.

**4:4** [...] He will not forsake them [...] and the seed of the wicked [...]

**4:5** shall be cut off forever.

**4:6** "The righteous-one shall inherit the land and dwell upon it

**4:7** forever" (Psalm 37:29).

**4:8** Its pesher concerns [...] for a thousand generations [...]

**4:9** to them and to their seed shall belong all the inheritance of Adam,

**4:10** and to their seed for ever.

**4:11** [...] the high mountain of Is[rael...].

**4:12** "The wicked-one watches the righteous-one and seeks to slay him.

**4:13** The LORD will not abandon him into his hand or let him be condemned when

**4:14** he is brought to trial" (Psalm 37:32-33).

**4:15** Its pesher concerns the Wicked [Priest] who watched the [Teacher of Righteous]ness and sought

**4:16** to slay him [...] and the Torah which he sent to him. But God will not abandon him and will not

**4:17** [condemn him when] he is brought to trial. And God will pay him his recompense by giving him

**4:18** into the hand of the ruthless-ones of the nations to do to him [...]

---

*EMET notes: Translated from 4Q171 Col. 4. The Wicked Priest (ha-kohen ha-rasha) appears explicitly at 4:15 — the great antagonist of the Teacher of Righteousness. "Inheritance of Adam" — alludes to the restoration of the primordial inheritance. "A thousand generations" — hyperbolic expression of permanence. The legal language at 4:16-17 suggests a formal trial. "Torah which he sent" — may refer to a halakhic letter (cf. 4QMMT).*
